capstone_read._doc: Capstone read, 2026-11-06: what in the Bernstein note is new to the wiki/registry, what contradicts our model or other sources on disk, and what is consistent. Our inferences are marked as such.

contradicts.t: Under-construction capacity is grandfathered in Bernstein's math; in ours it is not.
contradicts.d: Texas: 21 GW total / 16 GW credible "already under construction and grandfathered", so the at-risk set is unstarted capacity (2027: 0.3 GW credible; 2028: 5 GW). The reference deck (same Aterio base) delays 16.5 GW of campuses under construction, and our registry delays 6.0 GW (bear), mostly Texas phases already under construction whose on-site-gas air permit is pending (our TCEQ rule: "issued permits stand; the next power phase still needs approval"). The real disagreement is whether a pending permit for the next power phase stalls a building already rising.

contradicts.t: Texas construction starts sped up after the pause.
contradicts.d: Exhibit 28: 1.9 GW in Aug and 3.4 GW in Sep vs ~1 GW/month Jan-Jul; Exhibit 27: +5.3 GW under construction, +22.4 GW pipeline and only −0.4 GW stranded since Aug; Texas stayed ~28% of US starts. This cuts against FundaAI's 2-3 GW Texas 2027 IT cut (2026-11-04) and the deck's 9.2 GW of Texas delayed in 2026-28; it fits our registry's 0.9 GW Texas 2027 cut.

contradicts.t: Georgia: a pricing lever on 2030s load, not a stop on today's builds.
contradicts.d: PSC flipped 3-2 Democratic, but the ~10 GW certification and OpenAI's 3.2 GW contract are done; the sales-tax exemption runs through 2031 and repeal needs the Republican Senate; 87% of Georgia's pre-construction credible capacity is dated 2029+. Our bear case applies the deck's 6-month Bottoms pause (Jan-Jul 2027) to unstarted phases.

Spanberger kept the ~$1.9B sales-tax exemption and added a capped consumption tax. Our bear case assumes SB 843 passes (no new DC approvals 2027-07 → 2030-07), as the deck does; our own rules research rates it stress-only. Bernstein does not mention SB 843.

contradicts.t: Loudoun's 12-month pause: a vote on Nov 17, per Bernstein.
contradicts.d: Our local entry LOC-VA-011 records the Board pause as enacted 2026-09-16 (county release) and running to 2027-09. Either Nov 17 formalises a longer pause or it is a second instrument; if adopted, the end moves to ~Nov-2027. Check after the vote.

new.t: Pipeline exposure by company and state stance.
new.d: Share of under-construction + announced GW in restrictive/hostile states: AWS 59% (29.5 GW hostile alone), Microsoft 32%, Google ~29%, Meta 16%, Oracle 0%; Fermi 96%, MARA 100%, Galaxy 91%, Soluna 90%, Cipher 88%, Riot 87%; CoreWeave 36%, Nebius 33%, IREN 32%, Applied Digital 0%. Riot still rose 23% post-election: the market priced dependence on future approvals, not exposure.

~60 GW moved from Mostly Friendly/Cautious into Restrictive, Ohio and Georgia the biggest swings (Georgia's development multiplier 0.95x → 0.80x). Of the +27 GW credible, ~10 GW is under construction and grandfathered, leaving ~17 GW exposed: a 9% downside shock to the credible pipeline, 2-4% realistically.

new.t: Ohio's binding exposure is ~1.1 GW credible (Meta Piqua).
new.d: AWS Trenton (1.5 GW nameplate, ~1.1 GW credible) hinges on the Nov 10 St. Clair Township ban hearing; Prologis in Trenton is the closest thing to a true loss; projects leak to the next town (AWS ~2.8 GW elsewhere in Ohio). Our model already carries Piqua and Trenton (ballot bans) and St. Clair Township (moratorium in force since May-26), but none of these campuses is in the registry (no dated schedule), so Ohio locals delay 0 GW in the model.

new.t: Registry coverage per state vs Bernstein's under-construction capacity.
new.d: Texas: registry 15.2 GW of phases under construction (as reported) vs 21 GW (73%). Georgia: 1.1 GW vs ≥4.3 GW (top-22 players only; ~27%). Ohio: 2.2 GW vs ≥5.6 GW (~39%). Missing under-construction blocks Bernstein shows: AWS Georgia 515 MW, Digital Realty Georgia 354 MW, Microsoft Georgia 744 MW (our QTS Fairwater rows may carry part), EdgeConneX Ohio 731 MW, Aligned Ohio 494 MW, CleanSpark Georgia 249 MW.

new.t: Named campuses not in the registry (no dates yet).
new.d: Georgia: DLR Project Bunkhouse 2.0 GW, QTS Blakely 1.4 GW, Google White Oak + Rumble 2.7 GW. Ohio: Meta Piqua 1.1 GW, AWS Trenton 1.5 GW. Texas announced: Related Digital ~5.0 GW, Carlyle ~3.0 GW, Stream ~2.3 GW. Queued on the monitor backlog.

new.t: Ohio's "Company D" (8.0 GW announced) ≈ SB Energy's PORTS campus.
new.d: Capstone inference from the size match: our registry holds 8,024 MW for SB Energy/SoftBank PORTS (Piketon) vs Company D's 8,022 MW. Bernstein anonymises it.

Nov 10 St. Clair Township hearing (AWS Trenton); Nov 17 Effingham Camellia site plan and Loudoun pause; Nov 24 Ohio certification (Piqua); Dec 10 ERCOT audit; Dec 16 Louisiana PSC on Meta Hyperion; Dec 31 Georgia pricing docket / Ohio HB 646; Jan 12 Texas Legislature; Jan 19 Hinojosa; Mar 12 / May 31 Texas deadlines; Mar 31 Georgia session end; mid-2027 Georgia Power 2032-33 picks.

consistent.t: Basis: the deck counts campuses, Aterio counts buildings.
consistent.d: Bernstein's Texas under construction (21 GW, Aterio) vs the reference deck's Texas 35.1 GW (Aterio, "campuses under construction dated 2026-30") supports our earlier inference that the deck counts every dated phase of a campus under construction.

ERCOT audit to the PUCT Dec 10 and Hinojosa's approvals moratorium "until the Legislature passes new protections" ("the pause just got longer and maybe deeper") match our TX-ERCOT-LL and TX-HINOJOSA-MORATORIUM instruments; Bernstein's "until the Legislature acts could mean a while" leans to our bear end (Sep-27) or later.
Texas 2028 is "the most at risk" (18 GW total / 5 GW credible not started), as SemiAnalysis (2026-11-01) frames 2028 as the fight while 2027 is largely locked in.

caveats: Bernstein's Texas legs sum to 199 GW vs "~150GW of forward nameplate" in the same paragraph; the credible legs (16+0.3+5+8+22 = 51 GW) do match "~50GW likely to be built".
MW basis is not stated (Aterio nameplate). Registry comparisons use the registry's MW as reported (mixed bases) and its IT-equivalent.

Our Project Kilby rows (2.67 GW gen nameplate, Chevron power for a Microsoft campus) match "Microsoft" by developer text; Bernstein's Microsoft Texas bar has only 0.37 GW announced, so its source files Kilby elsewhere (or not at all).
